text: If your interviewer ever asks, "What is your greatest weakness?"... do not tell the truth.
Do not tell them about yourself. Never say you have no questions. And never wait for them to get back to you.
This is Instruction four four four.
There are four rules. Follow them exactly. Otherwise, you will have to activate the emergency protocol.
Rule one. Do not tell them about yourself.
"Tell me about yourself." They have already read your résumé. Three times. Every page.
They are not asking who you are. They are checking which version of you is safe to let out of the room.
Smile. Say your name. Say one sentence about your last job. Then stop.
Do not mention your hobbies. Do not mention your family. Do not say where you live.
The last candidate said she lived alone. The interviewer wrote it down.
Then he underlined it.
Rule two. Do not tell the truth.
Then the one in the middle leans forward. "What is your greatest weakness?"
The room goes quiet. The air conditioner stops. Even the clock waits.
Only two answers are allowed. "I work too hard." "I care too much."
Do not say procrastination. Do not say public speaking. Do not say you get nervous.
Whatever you say becomes your weakness. Forever. It goes in your file, and the file follows you.
A candidate once said, "I can't say no."
He has worked there for nine years. He has never gone home.
Rule three. Do not say you have no questions.
At the end, they put their pens down. "Do you have any questions for us?"
Never say no. In this room, the interview only ends when you ask something.
Say, "No, I think you covered everything," and the clock on the wall goes back to nine.
The one in the middle tilts his head. "Then let's start again. Tell me about yourself."
One candidate said no three times. He is still in that room. For him, it is still Monday, nine A.M.
Do not ask about the salary. Do not ask what happened to the last person in this role.
Ask only this. "When will I hear back?"
Rule four. Emergency protocol. How to fight back.
They stand up. "We'll get back to you."
They mean it. At three A.M., you wake up. Three interviewers are standing at the foot of your bed.
"We have a few more questions."
Here is what does not work.
Pretending to be asleep. They write down, "Lacks enthusiasm."
Saying you already took another offer. They ask for the company's name. Then they visit that company too.
Blocking their email. The next email comes from inside your house.
There is only one thing that works. Interview them.
Sit up. Fold your hands. Look the middle one in the eye. "So. What is your greatest weakness?"
The rules of that room apply to them too. They cannot lie.
The first one says, "Being asked questions." He gets smaller.
"Tell me about yourself." The second one starts to shake. There is nothing to tell. He gets smaller.
And the last question. "Why should I hire you?"
Nobody has ever asked them that. They fold up like paper, and slide out under your door.
One week later, an email.
"We regret to inform you that our interviewers have resigned. Would you like the position?"
Job title: Interviewer. Location: the chair.
And that was Instruction four four four.
If this ever happens to you... you know the protocol.
